scope: Durable acquisition lease/backoff, transactionally fenced cache success and preservation of existing manual Native capture.

before: A pre-query transport failure was not retained after restarting the runtime.
Independent runtime instances acquired Google data concurrently.
An old late query could overwrite a newer successfully saved snapshot.
Automatic repeated capture did not reuse the fresh matching complete snapshot.
after: Record the attempt before acquisition; persist bounded jittered retry metadata.
Acquire the owner/authority checked SQLite lease before network; force cannot steal a live lease.
Commit only the current unexpired lease together with complete encrypted cache/cursor/outbox.
Reuse only automatic matching horizons with the actually retained current manifest.

limits: Physical capture here uses a synthetic Google provider and actual Native crypto/storage plus local Rules.
Cross-runtime concurrency, expiry, rollback and corruption were validated with actual SQLite code, not injected into physical device processes.
The source runner retains phase4as in its filenames; these executions verify the Phase 4au implementation.
Automatic triggers, worker integration, total operation budgets and aggregate Phase 6 E2E remain unfinished.
No production Rules deployment, group migration, app reset, main merge, README overwrite or global UI polish.
